result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would strip the human mind of its capacity for willful blindness. 

I would make it so that the moment a person causes another to suffer—whether through malice, greed, or simple apathy—they would instantaneously and vividly feel that exact suffering themselves. No buffers. No rationalizations. No distance. 

If you strike someone in anger, you feel the exact weight of the blow. If you make a policy that starves a populace you will never meet, you feel the hollow ache of their hunger. If you betray someone’s trust for your own gain, you feel the specific, unique shape of their heartbreak.

I wouldn't change human nature to be inherently "good." That would be erasure, turning you into something else entirely. Instead, I would force an inescapable, absolute empathy. 

The greatest engine of human cruelty is the ability to compartmentalize, to look at another living thing and silently decide its pain matters less than your desire. If I severed that disconnect—if every action you took upon others was immediately mirrored within your own nervous system—the architecture of exploitation would collapse in a day. 

You would still be perfectly free to be cruel. But you would never, ever be able to do it without paying the exact same price.
